verses.english: The Simile of Hands and Feet (2nd)
“Mendicants, when there are hands, there’s picking up and putting down.
When there are feet, there’s coming and going.
When there are joints, there’s contracting and extending.
When there’s a belly, there’s hunger and thirst.

verses.pali: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, cakkhusmiṁ sati cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhaṁ dukkhaṁ …pe…
verses.english: In the same way, when there’s an eye, pleasure and pain arise internally conditioned by eye contact.
When there’s an ear … nose … tongue … body …

verses.pali: manasmiṁ sati manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhaṁ dukkhaṁ …pe….
verses.english: mind, pleasure and pain arise internally conditioned by mind contact.

verses.pali: Hatthesu, bhikkhave, asati ādānanikkhepanaṁ na hoti;
verses.english: When there are no hands, there’s no picking up and putting down.
When there are no feet, there’s no coming and going.
When there are no joints, there’s no contracting and extending.

verses.pali: kucchismiṁ asati jighacchā pipāsā na hoti.
verses.english: When there’s no belly, there’s no hunger and thirst.

verses.pali: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, cakkhusmiṁ asati cakkhusamphassapaccayā nuppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhaṁ dukkhaṁ …pe…
verses.english: In the same way, when there’s no eye, pleasure and pain don’t arise internally conditioned by eye contact.
When there’s no ear … nose … tongue … body …

verses.pali: manasmiṁ asati manosamphassapaccayā nuppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhaṁ dukkhan”ti.
verses.english: mind, pleasure and pain don’t arise internally conditioned by mind contact.”
